messages:
maya: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak we started seeing a small uptick in `OOM` rates on the 8xA100 pools, mostly long-context convos.

oliver: ah yikes. any obvious traces? KV-cache or workspace growth?

maya: looked at profiler snapshots. allocation churn spikes around token index ~1200 for long chats. workspace footprint grows then GC fires and keeps failing to reclaim contiguous slabs. attaching short dump: 
```
AllocatorReport:
  total_reserved: 36.0GB
  active: 28.2GB
  fragmented: 6.1GB
  largest_free_block: 14MB
  last_gc_succeeded: false
  knobs: expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=64, garbage_collection_threshold=0.6
```

sophie: that largest_free_block 14MB explains OOM with big KV slices. Max split 64mb might be too small so we fragment more.

ryan: did kernel change increase intermediate buffer counts? e.g., more temporary mats per layer?

maya: yes — kernel switch for fused-attn introduced one extra temp per head in a few layers. small but interacts badly with current splitsize policy.

oliver: can we try two quick experiments on a canary: 1) bump `max_split_size_mb` to 128 2) set `expandable_segments=false` to force coalesced allocation and rely on GC more aggressively?

maya: plan: run 24h canary with these knobs + increase `garbage_collection_threshold` from 0.6 -> 0.75. hoping fewer tiny free fragments and earlier GC.

deploy-bot: started canary deploy: canary-id=cny-2026-03-17-045, config ref: infra/canaries/pycuda-splits.json

ryan: also add an experiment where `expandable_segments=true` but we increase initial segment granularity so expansions are larger (reduce frequency). That might keep benefit of expandable segs without many tiny fragments.

maya: good idea. I'll add a run with `expandable_initial_mb=256` + `expandable_growth_factor=2`.

oliver: for observability please add the following metrics to the canary dashboard: `allocator.free_block_histogram`, `kvcache.largest_free`, `gc.run_duration_ms`, `oom.count` and token-latency p95.

maya: added. linking perf snapshot after 6h: https://redwood-internal/perf/3876543210/scan1 — shows fragmentation drop ~25% when `max_split_size_mb=128`.

sophie: nice. any cost on latency? bigger splits could increase risk of internal copying.

maya: p95 latency unchanged (~48ms) but memory growth smoother. GC runs slightly longer (~+12ms) but overall fewer fail GC attempts.

oliver: if this holds, we should adopt `max_split_size_mb=128` as default for long-context routes and add auto-tuner to bump it based on observed `largest_free_block` trend.

ryan: one caveat — on tiny-model hosts (single-GPU small mem) larger splits might waste reserved space. tune per-host-class.

maya: agreed. next steps: finish 24h canary, compare `expandable=false` vs `expandable_initial_mb=256` runs, then propose per-pool defaults + alert rule for `oom.rate > 0.1%`. I'll post a short PR with knob suggestions and quick playbook for oncall.

oliver: thanks — ping me when canary finishes and we can sync with SRE to roll to dedicated pools. :thumbsup:

maya: will do. stopping noisy verbose logs for now.

deploy-bot: canary finished: status=success (no increased OOMs) — full report at https://redwood-internal/reports/cny-2026-03-17-045

maya: excellent! moving to RFC for gradual rollout.
